title: Prompt weave routing runtime notes
content:
Purpose:
- Brain-dump of a small runtime-level component I sketched: a `Prompt Weave Router` that composes prompt fragments from multiple sources and routes pieces to different inference lanes (hosted, dedicated, local preproc, toolside).
- Goal: give app developers a single lightweight API for composing mixed-source prompts while enabling cost/latency-aware routing and partial evaluation caching.

High level idea (one-liner):
- A router accepts labeled fragments (system, user, memory, tool-output, retrieved-ctx) and outputs a composite execution plan that: 1) minimizes token cost under latency SLOs, 2) preserves provenance for audit/evals, 3) allows partial evaluation (precompute static pieces), and 4) supports fallback lanes.

Why this exists (real problems I hit):
- Apps want to include large memory blobs + short realtime data + tool output. Sending all of it to hosted model is expensive and often unnecessary.
- Need consistent provenance so we can show users what came from where and toggle parts in reruns/ablation.
- Want to be able to pre-evaluate or cache invariant fragments (e.g., user profile, policy blurb) and only send dynamic fragments.

API sketch (surface):
POST /v1/weave
Payload (JSON):
{
  "client_request_id": "str",
  "model": "rwd-4b-alpha",
  "fragments": [
    {"id":"f1","role":"system","text":"You are a helpful assistant.","weight":1.0,"static":true,"provenance":"policy-service/v2/123"},
    {"id":"f2","role":"memory","text":"user_pref: prefers concise answers","weight":0.6,"static":true,"cache_key":"mem:u:432"},
    {"id":"f3","role":"user","text":"What's the best itinerary for 3 days in Kyoto?","weight":1.0,"static":false},
    {"id":"f4","role":"tool","text":"weather(today): rain","weight":0.2,"static":false,"allow_truncate":true}
  ],
  "constraints": {"max_request_tokens":1200,"latency_slo_ms":150},
  "routing_hints": {"prefer_dedicated_for_long":false}
}

Response (planning-oriented):
{
  "weave_id":"weave_2026_02_20_ashapatel_7",
  "composite_hint":"system + memory + (user | tool) ...",
  "routing_plan":[
    {"fragment_id":"f1","lane":"cached-local","action":"reuse","est_tokens":10},
    {"fragment_id":"f2","lane":"cached-precalc","action":"attach","est_tokens":7,"cache_hit":true},
    {"fragment_id":"f3","lane":"hosted","action":"send","est_tokens":180},
    {"fragment_id":"f4","lane":"preprocess-local","action":"shorten_then_send","est_tokens":20}
  ],
  "aggregate_est_tokens":217,
  "decision_reasons":["cache hits for f1/f2","f3 dynamic -> hosted to preserve context"],
  "ttl_ms":60000
}

Lanes (quick taxonomy):
- cached-local: fast in-memory replacements (0ms extra), used for small static strings or user identity markers.
- cached-precalc: pre-evaluated embeddings or serialized prompt chunks kept in Redis/fast store. May be recomputed on policy change.
- preprocess-local: run short transforms (truncate, normalize, redact) client-side/edge proxy before sending.
- hosted: low-cost hosted model endpoint.
- dedicated: reserved GPU lane for predictable latency, more expensive but used when token budget high or model pinned.
- toolside: fragments handled by a tool adapter (code-exec, api-call) and returned as inline text or structured output.

Routing heuristics (first-pass):
- If fragment.static==true -> try cached-precalc (by cache_key) -> fallback cached-local -> incr tokens.
- If fragment.allow_truncate==true and (latency_slo tight or token budget low) -> apply heuristic truncation (keep leading 2 sentences + last sentence).
- If model==large and aggregate_est_tokens > max_request_tokens -> offload low-weight fragments to dedicated or summarize via a cheap model (rwd-1b-summarizer).
- If provenance contains "legal" or "policy" -> avoid truncation.

Partial evaluation & caching semantics:
- Cache keys: fragment.cache_key || sha256(fragment.text + fragment.role + provenance).
- Cache entry includes: rendered_prompt_piece, token_count, last_validated_at, validator_tag (policy hash).
- TTL default: 1 day; invalidation triggers: explicit policy update webhook, user profile change, manual purge.

Example internal sequence (ascii):
User -> edge-proxy: POST /v1/weave
edge-proxy -> weave-coordinator: normalize fragments, hit cache
weave-coordinator -> cache: lookup f2,f1
cache -> weave-coordinator: cache hits
weave-coordinator -> router-decider: plan lanes
router-decider -> runtime: dispatch preproc for f4
router-decider -> hosted: send f3 + attached pieces
hosted -> runtime -> weave-coordinator: tokens/resp
weave-coordinator -> edge-proxy: plan + execution metadata
edge-proxy -> client: response w/ weave_id + provenance header

Observability signals to emit for each weave call:
- weave_id, client_request_id, chosen_lanes, per-fragment token estimates, cache_hit_tags, decision_trace (short), end_to_end_latency_ms, model_used, fallback_triggered(Boolean)

Backward compatibility:
- This API is additive. Existing /v1/completions should still work. Weave returns a planning response and optionally triggers the full execution. We can support a parameter `execute=true|false` to just return plan for inspection.

Open tradeoffs / questions (notes-to-self):
- Where to put the decision logic? Lightweight rules in edge-proxy vs. centralized coordinator. Centralized simplifies experiments, edge reduces RTT.
- How much of partial evaluation should use a cheap on-device summarizer vs using cached raw text? Summary quality vs. provenance fidelity tension.
- Billing: if router triggers a summarizer step (cheap model) + hosted model, how attribute costs to customer? Need billing trace at fragment level.
- Security: fragments may contain PII. Cached-precalc store must support KMS/HSM integration for private deployments.

Experiment ideas / quick ABs:
- A/B region routing: route memory fragments to dedicated in region A vs hosted in region B and compare latencies and token spend.
- Cache warmup policy: keep top-100 user-profile fragments pre-warmed for high-activity accounts.
- Truncation heuristics: compare last-sentence-preserve vs prefix-only for tool outputs.

Implementation sketch (first cut):
- Coordinator: thin stateless service that: validates input, computes cache keys, queries Redis layer, runs routing rules, emits plan.
- Router engine (pluggable): rule engine in WASM so we can push updates without full deploy. Rules express lane preference and heuristics.
- Preproc workers: lightweight services collocated with edge-proxy to run quick transforms and summarize.
- Persistent cache: Redis for fast path (precalc blobs), S3 for large precomputed artifacts (e.g., long templates).

Short TODO list:
- [ ] Prototype JSON API + simple coordinator that does cache lookup and returns plan (no execute).
- [ ] Wire per-fragment metrics and a single trace/span for weave lifecycle.
- [ ] Draft security short: cache encryption + retention defaults.
- [ ] Discuss billing tagging with finance (how to break down model + summarizer costs per fragment).
- [ ] Spike: WASM rule engine feasibility.

Notes for future doc (if this sticks):
- Add examples of real product use-cases (CS assistant, travel planner, legal summarizer).
- Add deterministic replay model: store original fragments + plan so we can later re-execute with same decisions or run ablations.

Quick mental checklist before pushing to eng-infra for spike:
- Make sure we include a `execute=false` planning-only mode so UI teams can preview plan.
- Limit initial scope: only support 4 lanes (cached-local, cached-precalc, preprocess-local, hosted). Add dedicated, toolside later.
- Keep provenance visible in plan for UX debug.

Rough naming conventions:
- weave_id -> weave.<iso_ts>.<owner_short>.<n>
- fragment namespace: f:<short_role>:<sha8>

That's it for now — this is messy, intentionally. Next: prototype coordinator that returns `routing_plan` and a minimal decision trace.

Questions I want to ask Miguel in sync:
- Does Redis already have an LRU tier we can allocate for precalc blobs?
- Any objections to a short-lived TTL (1m) on plan objects for replay in tracing?

End.
